flows.goal: Create or mutate the current bass-slot line, inspect it and return to SEQ
route: Select the intended bass slot by an accepted K3 direction event, verifying the native owner.
Unused ARP tap enters TB-3PO; another ARP tap cycles its two pages. K2/ordinary page arrows clamp at either end in V_GEN.
GENERATE: K5 density, K6 accent, K7 slide, K8 octave range. SCALE: K5 root, K6 scale, K7 base octave, K8 auto-mutate interval.
OCTAVE+ immediately generates NEW LINE; OCTAVE− immediately MUTATEs. SEQ returns to step view. PATCH+REC invokes existing Undo only when its admission/history permits.
consequence: R_GEN controls except auto-mutate interval mark gen_stale; changing them prepares the next generation rather than rewriting the current line immediately.

NEW LINE resets all 64 step cells, including hidden cells beyond current length; generated velocity 0 resolves default 100. It generates only within active length and guarantees a note anchor if all generated gates are rests. UI clears all 64 chord and note-sound records.

MUTATE probabilistically changes only active-length steps and preserves an intentionally all-rest line. UI then clears all 64 chord records and note-sound entries whose cells are not NOTE. Manual mutate uses seed XOR wall time; visible stored seed alone does not reproduce the exact mutation history.
Length/rate/direction and unrelated motion are not claimed reset by these calls. Auto-mutate interval can mutate during playback at source traversal boundaries.

flows.goal: Find the actual engine-specific controls and assign a factory or pattern recall
route: PARA enters the remembered native sound page. K2 wraps through that engine's full page cycle; the trailing SOUND page is part of the current topology.
On SOUND K5 edits ENGINE, K6 edits PRESET; K7 is STATUS and K8 is unmapped. K4 is preset selection only in this exact SOUND context; elsewhere it cues patterns.
SEQ has a separate PRESET page: K5 assigns this pattern's bass recall, OFF or a bounded one-based factory value for the selected/requested bank.
consequence: Basic factory turns submit requests, not a universal inert browser or reversible audition. Native dynamic engine labels, existing ADSR/glyph pages and sparse columns already exist.

Per-pattern recall is stored in existing rsv[slot] byte. OFF makes no recall request. Invalid encodings remain invalid; numeric bounds come from original_sound_factories(kind), not stale comment counts.
pattern_sound_tick observes a cued/current pattern and its encoded value and requests recall once with that pattern gate. Actual completion/pending details remain with incumbent CP1.

flows.action_count: PARA = 1 press to remembered sound page; K2 page turns depend on remembered topology. One admitted PRESET turn submits a request. No fixed request-completion count or timing guarantee.

flows.goal: Preserve the live idea, distinguish request/result, or undo/reset only the intended sound
route: Short unused BT release requests project save. To reach readiness from RUN/REC, stop and disarm, then release actual note/transfer/clip owners; quiet and availability checks remain source-owned.
BT hold plus destination white key/pad performs the existing all-five-part copy route; occupied destination asks. Used BT release does not also save.
PATCH+REC and PATCH+PLAY invoke current Undo/Redo admission; they are not guaranteed take objects.

SMC HOME held plus eligible part SELECT opens RESET SOUND. It is factory reset of that part's sound, not loading the last durable sound. Its normal confirmation/cancel belongs to existing modal policy.
consequence: Source SAVED/UNSAVED/QUEUED/FAILED, SAVE AT STOP, REC OFF TO SAVE and SAVE WHEN QUIET already exist. Explicit save keeps the request until readiness; acknowledgment alone is not persistence.
Save failure leaves ui.dirty and sets save_failed. This is not a proof that every last durable object survives every write/power fault.
Copy takes each part from its actual current source slot and can report partial motion capacity; no audio snapshot or sample portability is implied.

RESET SOUND restores factory sound cells/tag with scoped history; preceding mixer edits are committed separately. Mixer level/pan/sends/mute remain. Readiness/undo capacity can refuse; current source can keep the question for retry.

After a project load is initiated by its reserved component, only a successful stage applies/reinitializes to 909 SEQ. Refusal/invalid stage keeps the existing project; this helper adds no Settings route.

flows.action_count: Unused BT tap/release = 1 save-request gesture. Copy = hold BT + destination press, plus occupied-destination confirmation when present. RESET SOUND admission needs HOME held + eligible part SELECT, followed by the actual question response.

flows.goal: Keep a captured controller target, shape a held effect and return to the original page
route: Physical SMC Pause Note 0x5D press while following captures targets immediately. Short press begun while locked peeks; a fresh locked hold ≥900 ms unlocks. MMC STOP remains transport.
Controller Page/knob banks and navigation remain source-owned; fader/knob targets can stay locked while buttons navigate.

On FX, each physical strip/button uses its current independent assignment. Hold one effect and use eligible arrow route to change that held assignment; ambiguous multiple holds consume arrows without remapping another target.
HOME held plus page-left/right selects ROOM/TIGHT/ECHO by source route. Current FX/navigation dual-role buttons may run FX while held; short taps can navigate.
BRK strip REC Note2 is momentary fill: request next 909 bar, show active only when fill_on&&fill_req, release or leavingFX ends it.
consequence: Pause captures target descriptors and selection bank, not transport pause. Lock can refuse during transaction/perf/question/clip contexts.
Peek lasts 1200 ms and restores prior UI/cursors; a second peer retains its original targets. Pickup remains distinct from ACTIVE.
FX release uses the original held bus/page/assignment. New selected page or another peer does not license ending unrelated effects.
REC buttons still toggle broad ui.rec; no exclusive future capture class is implied.

flows.goal: Enter host clip control, use the legal viewport and release exactly the original target
route: KNOB BANK rising press toggles clip mode when its current gate permits. It is not a hold gesture.
Fresh occupied pad press sends its visible cell's note with pad velocity; original clip_pad_note owns note-off even after viewport movement.
OCTAVE−/+ moves the bounded local viewport. Outside a menu, < > belongs to Clip Keys field editing, not viewport paging.
SCALE/CHORD/ARP presses open/close their current Clip Keys pages; opening a page is separate from its ON field. NOTE REPEAT+ARP toggles latch.
PLAY/REC send clip transport notes. PATCH+REC/PLAY sends Loopy Undo/Redo notes over USB for user binding, before ordinary UI transport.
Exit releases owned clip pad/key notes and disables Clip Keys modes per current source.
consequence: Sixteen physical pads view host APC cells; no off-viewport access or all-host-clips promise.
No host feedback and no Clip Keys page produces actual WAITING FOR LOOPY PRO / USB OR BLUETOOTH body.

Host palette/queued flags drive grid; visible viewport has white border and queued cells a dot. Local transport presses optimistically update local feedback, so a lamp does not prove host launch/recording.
Clip queued RGB can blink on accepted clock or 250 ms fallback; fallback is not measured host beat. No view-specific held RGB overlay is invented.

flows.goal: Retire the correct notes, release the chord and play a fresh phrase
route: Keyboard FX+SEQ chord requests instrument notes-off; both releases are consumed and both controls must be released before another panic can fire.
SMC BankL 0x2E+BankR 0x2F is panic only in explicit DAW mode with the hook enabled; USER and MMC are not that chord route.
In clip mode, unused NOTE REPEAT release runs ck_all_off, sends CC123 on the Clip Keys channel and shows PANIC. NOTE REPEAT+ARP is latch and consumes that standalone panic release.
Use PLAY/STOP separately when transport stop is desired. Fresh input after retirement must acquire its new owner.
consequence: Keyboard/SMC helper requests notes-off and does not change transport. It does not guarantee global silence, FX-tail cutoff or an external-device reset.
Current keyboard/SMC chord path does not itself display a dedicated PANIC receipt. Do not relabel the clip PANIC toast as a current universal keyboard screen.
Clip all-off flushes queued Clip Keys HUMAN onsets before their matching offs; it is not a promise that no MIDI is emitted.
Inactive mode/held-member changes inhibit false rearming. Old releases cannot be treated as a new panic chord.
current_reuse: Existing source header, current view and transport indication remain after consumed keyboard chord; this is evidence to retain, not a new status card.
